title: Quorum-backed rendezvous limiter for graceful regional spillover and proportional fairness
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a quorum-backed, rendezvous-hash routing layer for limiter state to enable graceful regional spillover when a local limiter is degraded or offline. The design couples small soft-state replicas (per-epoch token credits + tombstones) with an SLO-aware shedding policy so that requests are routed to the best available limiter copy while preserving proportional fairness across clients and minimizing head-of-line latency impact.
acceptance_criteria: Limiter state can be routed to at least 3 replicas using rendezvous hashing; quorum reads succeed for 99.9% of requests under normal conditions.
During a simulated regional outage, upstream traffic is rerouted to replica limiters and overall P95 tail latency for allowed tokens increases by < 25% for high-priority customers.
Fairness property: no client experiences sustained >2x relative deficit compared to baseline during 15-minute synthetic bursts.
Circuit breaker triggers (epoch-based) open within 10s of sustained replica failure and recover automatically with exponential backoff and advertised epoch updates.
End-to-end test harness, chaos tests, and a PRD + design doc are linked and reviewed by SRE and Security.
Grafana dashboards show bulk metrics: local versus replica spillover rate, token donation volume, per-customer deficit histograms, and SLO burn rate alerts
implementation_notes: Core idea: use rendezvous hashing to assign limiter shards (per-tenant or per-api-key) to a small set of replica limiters (N=3) to avoid global coordination hotspots.
Store only epoched deltas in soft-state (allocated credits, last-used timestamp, tombstone) to keep replication small and idempotent.

Quorum model: reads prefer local limiter; if local under degraded mode, perform a parallel quorum read (fast-path: majority of replicas). Writes use a primary write-back to local and async replication to others with causal epoch tags.
Fairness algorithm: proportional deficit round-robin with aging. When serving from replicas, deficit counters are normalized by client weight and aging window to avoid starvation.
Circuit breakers: epoch counters drive breaker state—if majority replicas mark a shard as degraded, open breaker for that shard and switch to emergency local soft-commit policy.
Emergency local overcommit: allow short-lived token overdrafts with repayment window and throttled token-donation to replicas when they come back up.
Security: all replica communication must be mTLS and integrate with KMS for ephemeral keys; audit logs must record spillover decisions for compliance.
Operational hooks: add per-shard trace IDs so we can trace a request's limiter decision across regions and replicas in the Console tracing UI.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: increased cross-region traffic during failover may cost more and create load cascades. Mitigation: rate-limit cross-region spillover and prefer same-region backup pools when available.
Risk: stale soft-state could allow short abuse window. Mitigation: tombstones + conservative repayment policy + short epoch durations (30s) with bounded clock skew assumptions.
Risk: complexity of proportional fairness math leading to oscillation. Mitigation: simulation harness and canary with traffic shadowing for 48h before rollout.
Risk: security surface expands for inter-replica comms. Mitigation: require security review, mTLS, and KMS integration; firewall rules to restrict replica endpoints.
testing_plan: Unit tests for rendezvous shard selection, epoch merge semantics, and deficit round-robin fairness invariants.
Integration tests: replica quorum reads/writes under normal, high-latency, and partitioned network conditions.
Chaos tests: kill local limiter process, simulate regional blackhole, and assert automatic spillover with bounded SLO impact.
Load tests: synthetic bursts of 10x baseline for 20 minutes to validate proportional fairness and repayment correctness.
Security tests: TLS mutual auth verification, replay attack simulation, and permission boundary validation for token-donation paths.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flagged rollout in staging. Shadow production traffic to validate deterministic shard mapping and performance (2 weeks).
Phase 2: canary in one non-critical region with 5% of traffic and 24h observation window. Enable detailed metrics and trace sampling.
Phase 3: progressive enablement (25%, 50%, 100%) for regions with available replicas; run 48h smoke tests at each step and allow manual rollback window.
Phase 4: global enable with SLO burn-in and two-week monitoring before marking Done.
observability_requirements: New Grafana panels: shard assignment heatmap, replica-quorum-latency (P50/P95/P99), spillover-rate-by-region, per-tenant deficit histogram.
Dashboards must link to traces for any request that performed a cross-region quorum read.
Alerting: SLO burn rate alert if cross-region spillover increases >5x baseline for 5m and P95 latency degrades >2x for critical tenants.
Audit logs: every limiter decision that used a replica or allowed an overdraft must be emitted to the audit stream with tenant id, epoch, reason code, and operator (service).
comments: 2026-02-10 Maya Chen: Created ticket after SRE blameless postmortem for incident INC-2026-01 (regional limiter outage). Proposed rendezvous+quorum approach to avoid single-leader hotspots.

2026-02-12 Diego Alvarez: Spike complete. Implemented prototype rendezvous mapper and simulated shard collisions. Observed 12% extra cross-region lookups with N=3; adding a same-region preference cut that to 3%.

2026-02-16 Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed prototype. Concern: token overdraft repayment could create sudden catchup bursts. Suggest implementation of leaky-bucket repayment throttles and telemetry to measure repayment velocity.

2026-02-18 Security review kickoff: Submitted initial threat model; required mTLS + KMS for replica comms. Security requested a short checklist for key rotation during failover (added to implementation notes).

2026-02-22 Jonas Müller (Product): Approved customer-impact plan. Proposed a tenant-exemption flag for large-enterprise customers with strict egress constraints to avoid cross-region spillover; we will add exemption metadata to the shard map.

2026-02-26 Diego Alvarez: Began implementation of proportional deficit queueing and epoch merging. Added feature flag and initial unit tests. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
2026-02-28 Maya Chen: Status update: integration tests in CI failing due to clock skew in Docker-based sim. Action: switch to controlled NTP-synced test harness; ETA 2026-03-03.
